scope: Proposition 4.6 (Interior estimate with a neck weight) of the manuscript “Bounded scalar curvature and smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow” (preprints/Bounded-scalar-curvature-and-smooth-extension-of-four-dimensional-Ricci-flow-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95655c4053c94f2b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Take any sequence of times with η(t) ̸= 0 and extract a tree as in Theorem 3.2. On its true compact and half-neck pieces in Bt(xt, D0a), let r be the physical length of the local regular patch, in I-units. For every fixed required derivative order j there are C, ν > 0 such that (r/a)2 |G|j,r(t) ≤ C H∗(t) + ϵ  e−νD . (4.21) Here D = 0 on compact pieces, including truncated outer compact regions. On a joining neck D, up to bounded shifts, is the minimum of the logarithmic distances from the two ends. It is the half-neck coordinate used in Section 2. Constants may depend on the extracted tree, and the exponent may be decreased.
